newsitem.title: UK: UK Channel 5 denies coverage problems.
newsitem.headline: UK Channel 5 denies coverage problems.

text.p: Britain's Channel 5 dismissed reports on Friday that less than half of the country was picking up its signal clearly.
The channel said it expected coverage of around 60 percent of the country at launch on March 30 and spokeswoman Sally Osman said "that is still the kind of figure we are looking at".
Trade newspaper Media Week reported this week that analysis of Channel 5's first week viewing figures indicated that only 40-45 percent of the country was getting a decent picture.

Osman said that households in some areas which Channel 5 had expected to fall outside its initial coverage area were reporting that they could pick it up. It is hoping to boost coverage to 85 percent of the country by the end of the year, when an extra broadcast frequency comes on stream. It plans to fill in the remaining gaps with cable and satellite carriage.
Pearson Television, a Channel 5 shareholder, has secured space on the Astra satellite system which it could make available to the new channel, enabling it to reach an extra 2.5 million homes.

Channel 5 this week secured a $142 million dollar movie deal with Warner Bros. The peaktime movie every weekday evening is the centrepiece of its schedule. -- Keith Weir, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8793
